description: Focus on applying AI, data analytics, and domain knowledge to solve complex real-world problems.
summary: Agrisata employs a data driven operations research technique to help farmers select the top few candidate rotation strategies that optimize their objectives while meeting farmer specified constraints. It liberates farmers from planning calculations and sieves out obviously infeasible or nonideal strategies. It has a farmer friendly interface which allows users to interact with the planning tool through a built-in chatbot. The suggestion made by Agrisata is not merely a list of rotation strategies, it provides rationale together with additional information which allows the user to make a better choice among the candidates through their own expertise.
details: Sideronostos, presented through our Agrisata “Field Shift” experience, is a farmer-centered decision-support tool that combines NASA Earth observation data with local soil information, crop characteristics, weather history, and farmer priorities to explore more resilient crop-rotation strategies. It analyzes indicators such as temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, vegetation stress, frost risk, and water availability, then compares multiple rotation options with explanations of their expected benefits, risks, evidence, and uncertainty. The project is designed to help farmers conserve water, improve soil health, reduce erosion and pest-cycle risks, and adapt to changing climate conditions while keeping local expertise central to every decision. We developed it with a Next.js and React frontend, a Python/FastAPI backend, TypeScript, geospatial mapping tools, NASA data services such as NASA POWER, GPM, SMAP, Landsat, MODIS, and SRTM, and an optimization model based on mixed-integer linear programming. Our creative approach combines scientific data, interactive maps, scenario comparison, explainable recommendations, and a conversational assistant in one practical workflow. We also considered data uncertainty, differences between satellite observations and ground measurements, farmer usability, equipment and market constraints, and the need to present recommendations as informed possibilities rather than automatic instructions.
